role: preserved real advisory comparison; not chosen as candidate-choice binding witness
current: Resource row -> canonical available form accepts from/until/quantity/attendees/amenities.
Result is one WorkspaceAvailability with echoed resource/interval/quantity/attendees, available bool, total/terms/refund cutoff.

Visible available result gates nested hold; hold prebinds echoed inputs, then independently checks email verification/customer/account/company roles/staff location/party rules/current free capacity and creates one frozen-price Booking.
dynamic_parent_overlap: from/until/quantity/attendees are real dynamic parents for advisory availability, and also hold inputs.
minimal_choice_binding_mismatch: WorkspaceAvailability is a scalar advisory contract, not Region[]/Employee[] candidate choices. It cannot supply hold.resource without an additional checked advisory/result projection contract; no singleton conversion/cast or broader binding is invented.

fair_alternatives.expected: Explicit check then hold; user rechecks after changing interval. Stale advisory never bypasses hold free/current authority guards.
Reuse available when canonical draft inputs complete, fence responses and display advice; final hold same schema/authority. Controller cost and custom read serving remain gates.
Does not represent this scalar result as candidate list; compare as applicability gap rather than claim a win.

open_cases: Canceled/out-of-order advisory responses cannot display old interval price as current.
Another booking after available=true makes final hold unavailable/conflict with no fabricated capacity.
Current customer or company-booker grant revocation rejects hold while public availability still reveals only allowed resource/price terms.
Changing amenities cannot silently remove required amenity advice; amenities is not a hold input, so final action must not imply a bound amenity promise absent a separate contract.
Lookup is advice, not reservation/payment/allowance confirmation.
stage: Full source retained; no CanRent runtime, compilation success or whole-app acceptance.
